text:
leo: starting canary rollout for runtime v2026.04.5 -> global 5% (chat-completions heavy). change window 09:00-11:00 UTC. will monitor for 30m.

deploy-bot: rollout_20260405_a1 started -> 5% global. Command: `/rollouts start rollout_20260405_a1 --version v2026.04.5 --percent 5` Logs: https://infra.redwood/rollouts/rollout_20260405_a1

nadia: quick FYI: dashboards show chat-completions error-rate +0.8% (baseline 0.3%). spike concentrated on route `/v1/chat/completions` in us-central. https://dash.redwood/alerts/2345

omar: digging traces — seeing a flurry of 500s with message: `kvcache-miss -> fallback sync` and long tail on worker queue. sample trace: `POST /v1/chat/completions -> worker-7`

srini: Is this present in staging? Any config drift?

nadia: staging fine. suspect interaction between new runtime's async batching and old KV client.

leo: can we isolate by routing only us-central traffic to canary and pin other regions back to stable? want to contain blast radius.

deploy-bot: Command queued: `/traffic split --rollout rollout_20260405_a1 --region us-central --percent 100` -> routing change will take ~30s

deploy-bot: traffic split applied -> canary now limited to us-central (5% overall, all canary impressions are from us-central).

omar: good — reproducing high 500s on us-central only. throwing a temporary hold. Recommend PAUSE and require ops signoff.

leo: pausing. `/rollouts pause rollout_20260405_a1 --by leo`

deploy-bot: rollout_20260405_a1 -> PAUSED at 5% (operator: leo).

release-manager: quick checklist: notify customer-facing teams if pause >15m, prepare a short blurb for status, and decide rollback vs config tweak.

srini: vote: :thumbsup: try a hotfix config first — bump `kvcache.max_concurrency` from 8 -> 16 in us-central canary pool, then resume 2% and observe. If errors persist, rollback.

omar: I can stage the config and run synthetic chat load against canary nodes. ETA 8m.

nadia: drafting status blurb: "Canary for runtime v2026.04.5 paused due to elevated `chat.completions` 500s in us-central. Engineers investigating; partners notified if extended."

[8m later]

omar: applied config change on canary nodes: `kvcache.max_concurrency=16` and restarted embed worker on the canary pool. Running synthetic at ~50rps to emulate heavy multi-turn.

deploy-bot: config_update_20260405_1 applied to canary nodes (us-central). Command: `/infra apply-config --pool canary-us-central --kvcache.max_concurrency 16`

nadia: immediate follow-up: error-rate dropped to +0.2% over baseline, p95 latency down ~70ms vs paused state. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/intra/chat-canary

srini: good signal. propose resume at 2% globally (us-central still host of canary), monitor 20m, then progress to 10% if stable. Vote?

release-manager: Vote: :raised_hands: resume to 2% probe. Update status page to reflect change.

leo: resuming small probe. `/rollouts resume rollout_20260405_a1 --percent 2`

deploy-bot: rollout_20260405_a1 -> RESUMED at 2% global (canary in us-central).

omar: synthetic and live traffic look OK so far; traces show kvcache hit-rate restored and queue depths normalizing.

nadia: i'll finalize the status blurb and add a note: "temporary config tweak applied; monitoring for 20m" and ping CS.

[20m later]

nadia: 20m probe complete. metrics stable: errors at baseline, latency within SLO. propose gradual advance to 10% over next 30m.

srini: agree. ops will keep enhanced traces on for canary nodes. If error-rate goes above 0.5% absolute increase or p95 regresses >100ms we auto-pause.

leo: let's proceed. `/rollouts update rollout_20260405_a1 --percent 10 --step 30m`

deploy-bot: rollout_20260405_a1 -> progressing to 10% over 30m with auto-pause triggers configured.

release-manager: release-note blurb (final): "v2026.04.5 gradual rollout: initial 5% canary paused due to elevated chat error rates in us-central; config fix applied and probe resumed. Continuing staged rollout with enhanced tracing." Link: https://tickets.redwood/INC-7890

leo: thanks team. keep an eye on the auto-pause triggers. i'll keep the change window open until 11:00 UTC.

srini: will follow up with a post-mortem doc capturing root cause (async batching <> legacy KV client), the permanent fix timeline, and recommended regression tests.

release-manager: marking this thread for post-release notes and customer comms. Good job isolating and avoiding full rollback.
